searchText: <@415548822983278593> if possible can you please provide a simpler summary for non eth devs who are curious about your findings in regards to miner profitability and 4488? 😀 as a miner I’m obviously curious I've never seen gas prices be so orderly weird they might be on the old fork Hilariously you may be correct 😂 Thanks Fixed. Also uncled ourselves again https://etherscan.io/block/13776850 Sure! So basically: Currently, mining software can be quite simple, because it just sorts all transactions it could include into the next block by payment, and then includes as many of them into the block as possible. This is the way geth implements it, anf you can’t really do any better if you would write your own mining software. The exception to that is of course MEV, where running modified mining software (namely mev-geth) is significantly more profitable. But at least mev-geth is open source. We really don’t want a situation where miners can have a big advantage by running some proprietary smart algorithm, because that would lead to centralization pressures over time. And so a concern with 4488 was: Because we now have 2 separate limits per block (calldata and gas), packing a block optimally with transactions could theoretically become a highly complicated challenge, and thus open the door to more profitable proprietary software. So I looked at how far from the theoretical optimum different strategies are. And turns out, there is this backlog method that gets you really close in profitability to that optimum. So as long as geth (and for after the merge all the other execution clients) just implement that one, that removes any incentive for people to write their own versions, and so removes that potential centralization pressure. Hope that makes sense? Indeed; the uncles hash would be a better example same with extra data, which is theoretically redundant with beacon chain graffiti And difficulty I would also say that box includes some deeper rethinks; for example, do we really need exec blocks to point to previous exec blocks when they are already contained inside beacon blocks that provide an ordering structure? Do we want to keep the two-layer structure in the long term at all? etc etc Oh also, fixing the whole "libp2p for consensus layer, devp2p for execution layer" thing should be in the purge somewhere, but I forgot about it Total sense 🙂 thanks Btw having used some optimistic rollups their gas fees are quite high but I’ve heard that’s because they aren’t fully released yet Hi! reposting from ethstaker, maybe some one here would know.. "I was once asked about getting slashings censorship data. I was told that ``Unless you were running a slasher at that time period, there is no way to historically determine there was censoring occurring for slashings being included in blocks.'' in response to using a distance proxy (i.e. slashing not occurring in slot N+1 after slashable offence happening in slot N). So, I was thinking about running a slasher actually and found this guide https://www.coincashew.com/coins/overview-eth/guide-or-how-to-setup-a-validator-on-eth2-mainnet/how-to-run-a-slasher. Do you Guys think that is a feasible option to get the data on censorship in slashings?" Would I need to stake in 32eth here to set up a validator in the mainnet using the above? <@194432762315407360> Would 4488 mean that L2’s in general take up less block space on eth1? In that case it could lead to a large gas decrease for a time period. The fork yesterday seems to have significantly decreased gas thanks to 3-4% more blocks a day. L2’s do use up a significant amount of block space. I don't know if it will lead to better block utilization or not The goal with EIP 4488 is to make rollup transactions cheaper. Because transaction data cost significantly less gas under 4488, it will increase the capacity of the block, sort of. Thank you for the explanation. Wish it could be estimated. Anyone here see / working with the cosmos community on gravity bridge chain? https://blog.cosmos.network/the-gravity-bridge-chain-is-coming-to-cosmos-7010ec7bd0ea

So basically: Currently, mining software can be quite simple, because it just sorts all transactions it could include into the next block by payment, and then includes as many of them into the block as possible. This is the way geth implements it, anf you can’t really do any better if you would write your own mining software. The exception to that is of course MEV, where running modified mining software (namely mev-geth) is significantly more profitable. But at least mev-geth is open source. We really don’t want a situation where miners can have a big advantage by running some proprietary smart algorithm, because that would lead to centralization pressures over time.

excerpts.author: ansgar.eth
excerpts.content: And so a concern with 4488 was: Because we now have 2 separate limits per block (calldata and gas), packing a block optimally with transactions could theoretically become a highly complicated challenge, and thus open the door to more profitable proprietary software. So I looked at how far from the theoretical optimum different strategies are. And turns out, there is this backlog method that gets you really close in profitability to that optimum. So as long as geth (and for after the merge all the other execution clients) just implement that one, that removes any incentive for people to write their own versions, and so removes that potential centralization pressure.
